message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 1978 | **The Shining** | Stanley Kubrick’s masterful psychological terror with iconic imagery. |
| 1980 | **The Thing** | John Carpenter’s tense, creature‑feature masterpiece set in Antarctica. |
| 1984 | **A Nightmare on Elm Street** | Wes Craven’s inventive slasher that introduced Freddy Krueger. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** | A chilling blend of crime thriller and psychological horror featuring Hannibal Lecter. |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** | Pioneered the found‑footage style, creating a genuinely unsettling atmosphere. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** | Danny Boyle’s fast‑moving zombie apocalypse that revitalized the genre. |
| 2004 | **Saw** | A gritty, puzzle‑based horror that sparked a long‑running franchise. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Low‑budget found‑footage film that made audiences feel like they were watching real hauntings. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** | James Wan’s supernatural thriller that blends folklore with modern scares. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both clever and genuinely scary. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” concept with a haunting soundtrack. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** | A slow‑burn, atmospheric period horror that’s unsettling in its realism. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** | Jordan Peele’s socially conscious horror that’s as smart as it is scary. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** | A tense, sound‑driven thriller that keeps you on edge. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** | Ari Aster’s daylight horror that turns a sunny festival into a nightmare. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** | A modern retelling of the classic tale with strong feminist undertones. |
| 2021 | **Candyman** | A reimagining of the 1992 classic that blends horror with social commentary. |
| 2022 | **The Black Phone** | A supernatural thriller that mixes creepy folklore with a modern twist. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** | A horror‑comedy about a murderous AI doll that’s both funny and frightening. |

Feel free to pick any that match your mood—whether you’re after psychological dread, supernatural chills, or a clever subversion of the genre. Enjoy the scares!
